key_points: The filing states the effective tax rate was 21.6 percent for 2022 and 24.6 percent for 2021.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 20 Income Taxes: rate reconciliation table
key_points: The U.S. statutory federal income tax rate was 21.0% in both 2022 and 2021, so the statutory baseline did not change year over year.
Tax settlements and lapse of statute of limitations was a (2.1)% item in 2022 versus (0.3)% in 2021, a 1.8 percentage point larger reduction — the largest single driver lowering the ETR.
Non-U.S. subsidiaries' earnings moved from a +1.1% addition in 2021 to a (0.1)% reduction in 2022, a 1.2 percentage point swing that lowered the ETR.
Tax credits and tax-exempt income was (0.9)% in 2022 versus (0.1)% in 2021, a 0.8 percentage point larger reduction.
State and local income taxes, net of federal benefit, was 3.1% in 2022 versus 3.0% in 2021 — essentially flat and not a driver of the ETR decline.
Valuation allowances were (0.1)% in 2022 versus nil in 2021, a negligible 0.1 percentage point effect (versus +4.0% in 2020).
Other was +0.7% in 2022 versus (0.1)% in 2021, a 0.8 percentage point item that pushed the ETR higher.
The reconciliation runs from the 21.0% statutory rate to actual tax rates of 21.6% (2022), 24.6% (2021) and 27.0% (2020).
Total income tax expense was $2,071 million in 2022, $2,629 million in 2021 and $1,161 million in 2020.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Note 20 Income Taxes: unrecognized tax benefits rollforward and interest/penalties
key_points: Settlements with tax authorities reduced unrecognized tax benefits by $74 million in 2022 versus $15 million in 2021.
Lapse of statute of limitations reduced unrecognized tax benefits by $104 million in 2022 versus $17 million in 2021.
Combined, settlements plus statute lapses reduced unrecognized tax benefits by $178 million in 2022 versus $32 million in 2021.
The unrecognized tax benefits balance fell from $1,024 million at December 31, 2021 to $962 million at December 31, 2022.
Increases for tax positions related to prior years were $30 million in 2022 versus $225 million in 2021.
Expenses for interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits were approximately $10 million in 2022, $40 million in 2021 and $260 million in 2020.
Of the $962 million of unrecognized tax benefits at year-end 2022, approximately $750 million would favorably affect the effective tax rate in a future period if recognized (2021: $780 million).

The company states it is reasonably possible unrecognized tax benefits could decrease within the next twelve months by as much as $150 million, principally from potential resolutions of prior years' tax items with various taxing authorities.

key_points: The retrieved p49 fragment (MD&A, following TABLE 4: EXPENSES SUMMARY) ends with the phrase 'recurring permanent tax benefits and the geographic mix of business.'

title: AMERICANEXPRESS_2022_10K — negative result: no FY2023+ effective tax rate guidance found in the document
key_points: Searches for forward-looking effective tax rate guidance ('effective tax rate expected 2023 range', 'outlook', 'guidance', 'business plan tax rate assumption') returned no AXP statement giving a numeric ETR expectation for 2023 or later.

All 2023-dated items retrieved relate to other matters: accounting standards effective January 1, 2023 (e.g., TDR/write-offs guidance), long-term debt maturity schedules, and retirement plan amendments effective January 1, 2023.
The 10-K therefore contains no quantified ETR guidance for FY2023 onward; this is a negative finding about the document, not proof that AXP gave no guidance elsewhere.
